:::{#thm-loocv-shortcut}
#### Leave-one-out cross-validation for least squares

For a linear model fitted by [ordinary least squares](correlation-regression.qmd#def-ols)
with every [leverage](#def-leverage) $\lev{i} < 1$,
the [leave-one-out estimate](#def-loocv)
can be computed from the single fit to all $n$ observations,
from its [fitted values](estimation.qmd#def-fitted-value) $\fitted_i$,
their [prediction errors](estimation.qmd#def-prediction-error)
$\prederr_i = \fitted_i - y_i$,
and the leverages:

$$
\cvest{n} = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i \in I} \sqf{\frac{\prederr_i}{1 - \lev{i}}}.
$$ {#eq-loocv-shortcut}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
#### Source

@james2021islr2e [sec. 5.1.2] states this formula for least squares linear or polynomial regression,
and @hastie2009elements [sec. 7.10.1] for many linear fitting methods.
:::

:::

::: proof
Not derived here;
see the sources named under the theorem.
The derivation needs a formula for how the inverse of the
[cross-product matrix](#def-cross-product-matrix) $A$
changes when one observation's outer product $\soprod{\termvec{i}}$ is removed from it
(the Sherman--Morrison formula),
which this page does not develop.
:::
